Ross Ice Shelf Project (RISP)
U. S. Antarctic Research Program
PART II
BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF ACTION AND ITS PURPOSE
The Ross Ice Shelf Project (RISP) is being conducted by the University of Nebraska on the Ross Ice Shelf in the Antarctic as a multiple year field operation. The main effort will involve drilling through the shelf to allow access to the water column and the sea floor below. The field effort of the first two years has employed explosion seismology and other surface geophysical and glaciological techniques to define details of a designated portion of the Ross Ice Shelf.
Several holes will be drilled: the first will be drilled to a depth of about 75 meters. Larger holes will then be drilled to allow access to the water and the sea floor beneath the ice shelf. Biological and ocean-ographic experiments in the sea water will then be possible. Drilling of the sea-floor bottom will also be done to remove sediment and rock samples.
